answer_text:
Let the general term be indexed by \(k\):

\[
T_{k+1}=\binom{n}{k}\left(\frac1x\right)^{n-k}(3x)^k
=\binom{n}{k}3^k x^{2k-n}.
\]

So the coefficient of the \((k+1)\)-th term is

\[
A_k=\binom{n}{k}3^k.
\]

The tenth term corresponds to \(k=9\). For its coefficient to be the largest, we need

\[
A_9 \ge A_8
\quad\text{and}\quad
A_9 \ge A_{10}.
\]

Now,

\[
\frac{A_9}{A_8}
=
\frac{\binom{n}{9}3^9}{\binom{n}{8}3^8}
=
\frac{n-8}{3}.
\]

Thus

\[
\frac{A_9}{A_8}\ge 1
\implies
\frac{n-8}{3}\ge 1
\implies
n\ge 11.
\]

Also,

\[
\frac{A_{10}}{A_9}
=
\frac{\binom{n}{10}3^{10}}{\binom{n}{9}3^9}
=
\frac{3(n-9)}{10}.
\]

Thus

\[
\frac{A_{10}}{A_9}\le 1
\implies
\frac{3(n-9)}{10}\le 1
\implies
3n-27\le 10
\implies
n\le 12.
\]

So \(n=11\) or \(n=12\).  
But for a term not containing \(x\), we need

\[
2k-n=0 \implies n \text{ even}.
\]

Hence

\[
n=12.
\]

Now find the term with no \(x\):

\[
2k-12=0 \implies k=6.
\]

The required term is

\[
\binom{12}{6}3^6
=
924\cdot 729
=
673596.
\]

\[
\boxed{673596}
\]
